key_insight: Progressively reason about object structure before estimating motion to decouple geometry and articulation, enabling stable monocular reconstruction of articulated 3D objects from a single image.
problem_solved: Monocular reconstruction of articulated 3D objects is unstable because motion cues and part structure are entangled; prior solutions rely on multi-view data, retrieval, or auxiliary video, reducing scalability and efficiency.
method: Progressive structural reasoning: infer coarse-to-fine part layouts and connectivity first, then regress articulation parameters conditioned on the recovered structure.
Joint geometry-and-motion optimization with articulation-aware priors and differentiable assembly to ensure consistent part shapes, joints, and plausible motions from a single image.
Lightweight monocular pipeline that avoids heavy multi-view supervision or retrieval, using self-consistency and structure-driven constraints to stabilize learning.
impact: Provides a scalable, efficient approach for single-image articulated 3D reconstruction useful for robotics, AR/VR, and animation; reduces data and compute requirements while improving stability of articulation estimates.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing progressive stages: image → part layout → part geometry → articulation regression → assembled 3D object
Before/after examples: raw image alongside reconstructed articulated mesh in multiple poses
Schematic illustrating decoupling of structure vs. motion (structure-first vs. direct regression)
Bar/line chart comparing reliance on supervision types (mono vs. multi-view/retrieval/video) and qualitative stability
paper_title: MonoArt: Progressive Structural Reasoning for Monocular Articulated 3D Reconstruction
paper_authors: Haitian Li, Haozhe Xie, Junxiang Xu, Beichen Wen, Fangzhou Hong
